messages:
morgan: quick check-in — ran the mixed-precision bakeoff on the new 70B-bridge model. saw a weird long-context degradation around 1.3% rouge-L when at 8k tokens for some prompts. suspect per-head outliers on layers 32-34.

anika: can you paste the quick diff and the eval harness command?

morgan: sure, here is the run command we used:```./bench_eval.py --model bridge-70b --quant awq-int8 --seq 8192 --evalset longform --n=500``` got these stats: baseline fp16: 0.0% delta, awq-int8 default: -1.26% rouge-L, awq-int8 +kl-rescale: -0.48% rouge-L.

raj: interesting. did you try headwise mixed precision or just blanket layer quant?

morgan: just blanket initially. tried a quick headwise probe where we force FP8 for top-k offending heads per layer (k=3) and INT8 elsewhere: result ~ -0.12% rouge-L, perf drop ~4% throughput.

taylor: that sounds promising. what's your detection rule for "offending" heads?

morgan: ETA: compute per-head activation MAD over eval set, then mark heads with z>6 as outliers. snippet:```# pseudo
mad = median(abs(x - median(x)))
z = (x - median)/ (mad*1.4826)
bad_heads = where(z>6)
```

anika: nice. any idea if those heads are stable across seeds / prompts or just some prompts?

morgan: mostly stable across seeds, but spikes in a subset of prompts (long dialogue history) — so it's correlated with context length.

raj: i'd worry about operational complexity if we maintain per-head profiles per model version. maybe we can do a lightweight runtime check for high-kv magnitudes and route to FP8 path on the fly?

taylor: runtime gating adds latency. alternative: precompute head-rescue masks per model version + store in model metadata. then runtime just checks a flag in the request with little overhead.

morgan: agreed. for now we generated a rescue mask file and attached fallback policy: if seq_len > 2048 and sample triggers >2 bad heads active, switch to rescue-mask quant config.

anika: any eval on generation quality other than rouge? ppl, attr scores?

morgan: ran ppl on longform set: fp16 12.8, int8-blk 13.9, headwise-rescue 13.0. containment looks OK. also ran a small hallucination eval — headwise-rescue reduced hallucination rate from 7.6% to 6.9%.

raj: what's the rollout plan? can we A/B test on dedicated capacity?

morgan: plan: canary on dedicated pool with 5% traffic using rescue-mask + metrics dashboard: rouge-L, ppl, token-latency, cost-per-token. if regression <0.2% and latency hit <8% we promote.

quant-bot: auto-run scheduled: https://ci.redwood/quant/bakeoffs/2098754321. DAG: quant-probe -> head-stats -> eval -> artifacts/upload.

taylor: a couple followups: 1) try a looser MAD threshold (z>4) to capture more heads, see tradeoff; 2) test hybrid AWQ+gptq (weights gptq for attn, awq for mlp) for throughput/quality sweet spot.

morgan: noted. i'll queue both experiments. @raj can you add a dashboard panel for per-layer head-fraction-rescued and a heatmap by prompt-length?

raj: on it, adding panel and alert if rescue fraction >0.3 for more than 10m.

anika: thanks — can you also stash the rescue masks under model:/artifacts/bridge-70b/rescue-masks/ with semantic name (seq-bucket, date, threshold) so ops can apply versioned masks?

morgan: done, I uploaded 2098754321-mask-z6-seq8192.json to that path.

deploy-bot: deploy queued to dedicated-canary (5%) — build 2098754321. Logs: queued -> staging -> running.

morgan: will post a short writeup and the eval plots once the looser threshold run completes. thanks all for quick feedback :thumbsup:
